samples.summary: Format painter copies structural inline keys (`image`, `pageNumber`, `href`); pasting them merges an image/page-number/link onto every run of the target selection
samples.evidence: `captureFormatAtCursor()` returns `{ ...raw, bold, italic, ... }` where `raw = caretInlineStyle(...)` is the caret run's *entire* style object. `InlineStyle` includes the structural keys `image?: ImageData`, `pageNumber?: boolean` and `href?: string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:191-193) — note `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` deliberately omits `image`/`pageNumber` "they are structural inline kinds, not character formatting" (types.ts:256-258), but the painter does not. `pasteFormat()` (text-editor.ts:405) hands the whole buffer to `applyStyleToSelection` -> `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, which merges it into every slice. `layout.ts:777` then treats any run with `style.image` as a single unbreakable image segment spanning the run's text, so the target text stops rendering and the image is duplicated for each restyled run. Reachable in normal use: place the caret immediately after an inline image (`caretInlineStyle` returns the image run's style for an offset equal to that run's end, caret-style.ts:59), press the new Format painter button, select text, press again. `href` has the same shape: painting from a link silently hyperlinks the target. This behaviour predates the diff (the Mod+Shift+C path), but the diff promotes it to a public `EditorAPI` and a toolbar button, which is what makes it easy to hit.

samples.summary: copyFormat() picks the format up from the caret, not from the selection — a backward (right-to-left) selection copies the run *before* the source text
samples.evidence: `copyFormat()` calls `captureFormatAtCursor()`, which reads `caretInlineStyle(this.doc, this.cursor.position)`. For a backward selection the caret sits at the range start, and `caretInlineStyle`'s `position.offset <= inlineEnd` test resolves the run *preceding* that offset when the offset falls on a run boundary — exactly the caret-vs-range hazard `isStyleOnInSelection` documents for issue #715 (text-editor.ts:3333-3347). The toolbar flow the diff adds is "select the source text, then press the button", so a right-to-left drag over the source picks up the wrong format with no feedback. The range-based summary (`getRangeStyleSummary`/`visitStyledRunsInRange`) is the walk the rest of the editor uses for this question.

samples.summary: `editor.focus()` is called synchronously with the dialog close, so Radix's FocusScope restore is likely to steal focus back to the trigger
samples.evidence: `handleSubmit` does `onOpenChange(false); editor.focus();`. Radix Dialog restores focus to the trigger during its FocusScope teardown, which runs after this call. The same repo documents the hazard and the fix at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:358-360 ("Defer the slim-toolbar alignment commit to onCloseAutoFocus ... so `editor.focus()` runs after Radix's FocusScope teardown and sticks, instead of the scope stealing focus back to the trigger") and uses `onCloseAutoFocus` at lines 596/618/641. Result: after applying a page setup the caret is not returned to the canvas and the next keystroke goes nowhere. jsdom does not model FocusScope restore, so the new tests cannot see this.

samples.summary: Mobile overflow menu opens the Page Setup dialog from a DropdownMenuItem's default onSelect — the menu's close/focus-restore races the dialog mount
samples.evidence: `<DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => setPageSetupOpen(true)}>` does not `preventDefault()` the select, so Radix closes the menu (restoring focus to the trigger and tearing down its modal pointer-events layer) in the same tick the Dialog mounts and grabs focus. This is the standard Radix menu→dialog race: focus can end up back on the overflow trigger and, in the bad interleaving, `document.body` is left with `pointer-events: none` from the dismissed menu layer, making the dialog non-interactive. Every other item in this menu either mutates the editor synchronously or uses `onSelect={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`; none of them opens a dialog, so there is no precedent in this file. Only the desktop path is covered by the new test (`is reachable from the docs toolbar`), which renders with `isMobile === false`.

samples.summary: Margin round-trip is lossy at the 1px level: a seeded value is re-applied as a slightly different pixel margin
samples.evidence: `toInches` renders `px/96` at two decimals (0.01 in = 0.96 px) and `parseInches` re-multiplies with `Math.round`. A ruler-dragged margin such as 99 px displays as "1.03" and, if the user applies without touching that field, is written back as `Math.round(1.03 * 96) = 99` — fine here, but the mapping is not injective in general (values differing by <1px collapse), so opening and applying the dialog can silently shift an untouched margin by a pixel and produce an undo step for a change the user did not make.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end in the repo. captureFormatAtCursor() (text-editor.ts:3306-3320) spreads `raw` = getStyleAtCursor() = caretInlineStyle(...) (text-editor.ts:3287-3289; caret-style.ts:46-66), which returns the caret run's entire style object including the structural keys `href`, `pageNumber`, `image` (types.ts:191-193). Only the six boolean keys are normalized; nothing strips structural keys — unlike CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, which deliberately omits `image`/`pageNumber` as "structural inline kinds, not character formatting" (types.ts:253-260). pasteFormat() (text-editor.ts:399-407) hands the whole buffer to applyStyleToSelection (3259-3278) -> Doc.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:407-412) -> MemDocStore.applyStyle (memory.ts:219-222) -> block-helpers applyInlineStyle (426-476) -> mergeInlineStyle (390-399), a plain `{...base, ...patch}` spread; styleOffAsClear only rewrites boolean keys, and normalizeStyleClears/resolveScriptExclusion do not touch image/href/pageNumber. Layout then treats any run with style.image as one unbreakable image segment spanning the run's text (layout.ts:777-790), so painted text stops rendering and the image is duplicated per restyled run; `href` silently hyperlinks the target. Reachable in normal use: caret-style.ts:59 uses `position.offset <= inlineEnd`, so a caret at the end of an image run (or anywhere inside a link run) resolves to that run's style, and both the Mod+Shift+C/Mod+Alt+V handler (text-editor.ts:1205) and the new public EditorAPI/toolbar button (editor.ts:2904-2913; packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:127) drive it. Existing tests (test/view/editor-format-painter.test.ts) only assert bold/fontSize and do not guard this. Real correctness defect (content corruption / broken run invariants) on a normally reachable path.
